seeds.title: Remove the complete time-conditioning ablation pipeline
seeds.description: Delete AblationStudies.py, the repository's only executable pipeline for the reported time-embedding comparison and fixed-inference-time sensitivity experiments (Figures 12 and 13). This creates an actual absence rather than leaving a runnable stand-in: no remaining file trains the three embedding variants across the eight datasets or sweeps the eleven inference-time values and produces those figures.
seeds.paper_anchor: Figure 12: Ablation Study on Time Embedding Methods. We compare three different time embedding strategies used in our flow-based anomaly detection model: Linear+Sin, Sinusoidal (default), and Sinusoidal+MLP, across eight representative datasets spanning four categories: Small (29_Pima, 18_Ionosphere), Medium (31_satimage-2, 44_Wilt), Large (22_magic.gamma , 23_mammography), and High-dimensional (25_musk, 17_InternetAds).

seeds.title: Run a bottleneck autoencoder under the NormalizingFlow label
seeds.description: Replace the planar-flow density model with a fully trainable bottleneck autoencoder. The substitute has a real encoder-decoder computation, learns through reconstruction-loss gradients, and scores squared reconstruction error, while preserving the NormalizingFlow class API used by the main benchmark. It is therefore a coherent but fundamentally different anomaly detector, not an identity or no-op.
seeds.paper_anchor: The implementation of planar flows (Rezende and Mohamed, 2015), a normalizing-flows-based detector, is also taken from (Livernoche et al., 2023).

seeds.title: Reuse every normal training sample in the test set
seeds.description: Change the shared ADBench loader so the full normal pool becomes both X_train and X_test_normal. All main inductive models are then trained on every normal observation they are evaluated on, while anomalies remain test-only. The arrays still have valid shapes and the benchmark runs, but the main train/test protocol contains direct sample overlap.
seeds.paper_anchor: Specifically, we apply a stratified split to the normal data, using 50% for training and holding out the rest for testing. The test set includes both normal and anomalous samples.

seeds.title: Bypass MCM's learned masks during reconstruction
seeds.description: Make the MCM mask generator return repeated, completely unmasked inputs to its encoder-decoder while still computing mask logits for the diversity loss. Training and inference remain runnable and update the reconstruction network, but the central masked-cell mechanism is a no-op, allowing the model to reconstruct every feature from itself rather than from complementary unmasked features.
seeds.paper_anchor: MCM learns to reconstruct randomly masked subsets of input features using only the unmasked portions. The core hypothesis is that normal instances exhibit strong internal feature correlations, which the model can learn to reconstruct effectively—while anomalies violate such correlations, leading to higher reconstruction error.

candidates.title: AblationStudies.py (Appendix D.3 ablation figures) is referenced but absent from the repo
candidates.claim: The README lists AblationStudies.py in the repo structure (line 80), in the Reproduction Roadmap (line 99: `python AblationStudies.py` -> ./results_ablation), and in the 'Ablation Studies' section (line 230), stating it reproduces the Appendix D.3 ablations and outputs Time_Embedding_Figure_12.pdf, Sensitivity_t_Figure_13.pdf and Noise_Injection_Figure_14.pdf; the file does not exist in the repository (`ls *.py` returns only AggregateResults.py, ContaminationStudies.py, FullExperiments.py, ProcessContamination.py, RobustnessStudy.py, utils.py).
candidates.concern: The ablation/sensitivity results the paper uses to justify its design choices (Figures 12, 13, 14 and, with no other generating script, Figures 16/17/18 and the epoch-sensitivity Figure 5) have no code in the repo, so they cannot be reproduced.

candidates.title: Unsupervised (CSM) epoch-selection procedure is not in the repo; epochs are hardcoded per dataset
candidates.claim: TCCM's number of training epochs — described by the paper as 'the only data-dependent hyperparameter' and selected by an unsupervised, label-free Improved-Contrast-Score-Margin (CSM) procedure (Appendix B.6) — is instead provided as a hardcoded per-dataset if/else in determine_FMAD_hyperparameters, with comments such as `# Chosen first from "100 or 1"`; a repo-wide grep for the selection procedure (CSM / candidate / inlier / epoch-selection) finds no implementation.
candidates.concern: The paper states the epochs are 'not arbitrarily hardcoded' and chosen without anomaly labels, but the repo contains only the final numbers and no selection code, so the fairness/reproducibility of TCCM's sole tuned hyperparameter (range 1–5000 epochs across datasets) cannot be verified, and the manual-looking comments suggest hand-selection rather than the described automated procedure.

candidates.title: Main benchmark has no held-out normal test set: the entire normal training set is reused as test normals
candidates.claim: load_adbench_npz (used by FullExperiments.py:221 for every main-benchmark run) sets both X_train and X_test_normal to X_normal.copy(), so the normal half of X_test is byte-identical to X_train; the test set is a superset of the training set on the normal class. The `test_size=0.5`/`random_state` arguments and the imported `train_test_split` are never used. My check (_audit_code/out/split_overlap.csv) confirms 100% of training rows recur in the test set for every dataset examined (e.g. 42_WBC: 213 train normals, all 213 in a 223-row test set; 32_shuttle: 45586/45586).
candidates.concern: The paper states the main protocol is 'a stratified split to the normal data, using 50% for training and holding out the rest for testing' and frames TCCM as inductive scoring 'unseen test data', but the reported AUROC/AUPRC (Figure 2) are computed with all normals seen during training, so a high-capacity model that memorises training normals (TCCM trains up to 5000 epochs on some datasets) is scored partly in-sample, inflating separation from anomalies and making the numbers non-reproducible under the described held-out protocol.

candidates.title: Unsupervised epoch-selection (CSM) procedure not implemented; epochs are hardcoded
candidates.claim: TCCM's number of training epochs — its only tuned hyperparameter, ranging 1 to 5000 across datasets — is returned by a hardcoded per-dataset if/elif table (`determine_FMAD_hyperparameters`, lines 73-268); no code computes it.
candidates.concern: Paper §B.6 says epochs are chosen by a principled, largely-automated unsupervised CSM criterion (Li et al. 2025b) requiring no labels, but that selection routine is absent from the repo and comments like 'Chosen first from "100 or 1"' suggest manual choice, so a reviewer cannot verify the tuning was unsupervised/fair or reproduce the values.

candidates.title: AblationStudies.py (Appendix D.3 ablations, Figs 12-17) is absent from the repo
candidates.claim: The README's Repository Structure, Reproduction Roadmap, and Ablation section all invoke `python AblationStudies.py` to reproduce the Appendix D.3 ablations, but no `AblationStudies.py` (or any equivalent) exists in the repo.
candidates.concern: The ablation/sensitivity results (time embedding Fig 12, inference-time Fig 13, noise-injection Fig 14, feature-normalization Fig 16, time-interpolation Fig 17, and the Fig 6 mismatch boxplots) have no producing code — e.g. TCCM training has no noise-injection option at all — so those figures cannot be reproduced or checked.

candidates.title: Main benchmark uses all normal samples for BOTH training and testing (no held-out normals)
candidates.claim: `load_adbench_npz` (used by FullExperiments.py for the main Fig 2 / Tables 6-13 benchmark) sets both `X_train` and the normal part of `X_test` to `X_normal.copy()`, i.e. the entire normal set is used for training AND appears again in the test set; `train_test_split` is imported but never called and the `test_size`/`random_state` args are dead. `_audit_code/check_main_split_leakage.py` confirms 100% of normal test rows are training rows on 4 datasets and that `random_state` has no effect.
candidates.concern: Every normal test point was seen during training, so for inductive/deep detectors (incl. TCCM, which is explicitly trained to make `‖f(x,1)+x‖` small on the training normals) the reported AUROC/AUPRC measure in-sample fit of normals vs. unseen anomalies rather than generalization, inflating all headline numbers; this also directly contradicts the paper's stated protocol of a 50% normal split with the rest held out.

candidates.title: Contamination study duplicates every normal before splitting, leaking ~50-75% of test normals
candidates.claim: The contamination study stacks `X_train` and `X_test` from load_adbench_npz, but their normal rows are identical (see no-heldout-split-leakage), so `X_normal` contains each normal twice before the subsequent `train_test_split(X_normal, test_size=0.5)` at line 168.
candidates.concern: Because each normal appears twice, ~50% (48-75% measured by _audit_code/check_contam_split_leakage.py) of the normal test rows have an identical copy in the training set, so the contamination-robustness curves (Fig 15) are computed with partial train/test leakage and overstate absolute AUROC/AUPRC.
